requirements.requirement: A usable website exists, with an associated repository containing the website's source code. Record both links and the deployed source revision.

Everything in the playground demo is public by default, including the website, source repository, runs/results, live demos, recordings, replays/history, simulation outputs and supporting evidence. Any nonpublic exception reflects an explicit user instruction or visibility change, recorded below.

The website clearly names the actual approach/method being run. Use the executed method's name; Spotter is an example, not a shared hardcoded label. The **Model** field identifies the approach being tested, as specified below.
When a human joins, collect or confirm their name and email. Prefill known identity/default values where available and let the runner edit both fields before joining.
Run context includes the actual approach and confirmed runner identity; the website makes clear which method is running and whose run it is.

Policy/model tests initiated by a person retain that actual user's confirmed name as runner. Use available identity and editable name/email defaults; require the real name to be provided/confirmed if missing before testing or running. Do not substitute `Anonymous`, `Autonomous` or `Automated` for that person. Record execution mode (such as `automated test`) and actual approach separately from human identity. Genuinely unattended/system activity has an explicit system identity; never fabricate a person's name or email.
A person can use the website to run the integrated paper's method on physical YAM robots/arms. Record a verified physical execution of that method.
The actual physical arms are visible live on the website while the method runs, so a visitor can see that it is executing on real hardware.
Immediately after a run finishes, the person can replay that just-completed physical YAM execution through the website, with retained footage showing the actual arms executing the integrated method.

The person can browse/select previous runs on the website and replay their retained physical arm footage, associated with the executed method and run. Mock animations do not satisfy either replay requirement.

If the integrated method executes anything in simulation, those executions are reviewable within the integration website and tied to the corresponding run. A reviewer can inspect what ran and its results using suitable replay/visualization and relevant outputs, as appropriate to the simulation. Clearly label simulation content to distinguish it from physical-arm footage. If nothing executes in simulation, record an explicit not-applicable explanation instead of claiming simulation review.
The website is intuitive: a new visitor, without coaching, can find how to run the method. Record the visitor path and starting conditions; site entry has no separate 15-second pass/fail deadline.

**Mandatory for every run:** first observed actual method-driven physical YAM motion occurs both within **15 seconds after the startup move to Home completes** and within **30 seconds after the Run click**, using the boundaries below (including a documented readiness timestamp when Home is unnecessary). Homing/preparation motion does not count. Verify and record both full elapsed times for every run; a sampled demonstration is insufficient. Apply only the documented GPU-launch or research-grounded exceptions below.

Every meaningful wait after a website action is immediately explained in a persistent inline status/progress area at that action (below Run in the run panel for launches). Show the current stage, a plain-language reason and real stage completion, with honest failure/stall status and available recovery. Verify the detailed wait-stage behavior below.

Before marking the integration complete or reporting it done, open the deployed website and perform a final end-to-end physical YAM run through its normal user interface. Verify every completion requirement against that deployment and record evidence; unmet or unverified requirements block completion.
